What if one video game could switch off the planet? On November 19th, it might try.
Around 130 million PlayStations and Xboxes could wake up at once, each pulling about 200 watts.
And power grids are more fragile than you think.
In 2003, one tree branch touched one power line in Ohio. 50 million people lost power.
In 2021, Texas froze, and its grid came 4 minutes and 37 seconds from a blackout that could have lasted months.
In 2020, India switched its lights off for just 9 minutes. Demand dropped 31 gigawatts, more than double what engineers expected.
Now flip it. 130 million consoles at 200 watts is about 26 gigawatts, all switching on together.
If the grid can't keep up, the frequency drops. Power stations trip off to protect themselves, and the lights go out, block by block.
130 million players, sitting in the dark, four minutes into the game they waited 13 years for. And nobody saved.
So could GTA 6 really black out the planet? Probably not. Not everyone plays at midnight, and the load is spread across countries and time zones.
But last time, it only took one tree. And Ohio has a lot of trees.
